name: Socket/switch board wiring

steps.title: Power isolated and verified
steps.visual_criteria: Main isolator switch is OFF, neon tester shows no voltage on terminals

steps.title: Insulation stripped cleanly
steps.visual_criteria: Wires stripped 10-12mm without nicking or cutting copper core strands

steps.title: Phase and neutral polarity connected
steps.visual_criteria: Phase wire (red) into switch/L terminal, neutral (black) into N terminal

steps.title: Earth wire bonded securely
steps.visual_criteria: Green earth wire firmly connected to top ground pin terminal

steps.title: Terminal tightness and cover fitment
steps.visual_criteria: Screws tight with no bare copper exposed outside terminals; faceplate secured

scenario_questions.text: What do you check before touching the wires or terminals on a switchboard?
expected_points: Isolate main power switch or MCB
Verify absence of voltage with a neon tester or multimeter

scenario_questions.text: Why must the phase wire always pass through the switch instead of the neutral wire?
expected_points: Cutting phase disconnects live voltage from the appliance
Prevents electric shock when appliance is turned off

scenario_questions.text: What should you do if the earth wire is broken or missing in the conduit?
expected_points: Do not leave the board ungrounded
Inform homeowner/contractor and pull a new continuous earth wire

common_mistakes: Not testing for voltage before touching terminals
Connecting phase wire directly to socket without switch control
Leaving exposed bare conductor outside terminal blocks
Loose screw connections causing terminal sparking
